To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ROS produced by the mTAL are important determinants of blood flow, sodium excretory ability, and blood pressure in the rat.
ROS are important determinants of mTAL Na(+) re-absorption and medullary blood perfusion, and that these two functions of ROS are important in long-term regulation of arterial blood pressure.
excess ROS production in the mTAL of the SS rat results in medullary hypoperfusion, which contributes to the development of hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms by which excess sodium delivery to the renal medulla, and the resultant increase in ROS, leads to hypertension.
the role of the renal medullar thick ascending limbs of the loop of Henle in the control of sodium homeostasis and long-term control blood pressure.
the role of ROS and redox signaling in medullary blood supply, sodium excretion and hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ROS production by the mTAL, and the resulting medullary ischemic state, is a key factor in salt-sensitive hypertension.
ROS production in the mTAL is a major contributor to salt-induced hypertension.
ROS are important determinants of renal medullary blood perfusion, sodium reabsorption, sodium homeostatic control, and blood pressure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ROS produced in the mTAL in the SS rat are not only responsible for medullary vasoconstriction but also for enhanced Na(+) and water reabsorption in this segment of the nephron, resulting in the development of hypertension.
the mTAL is a major source for the production of ROS, which in turn regulate the balance between medullary perfusion and sodium excretion.
the ROS generated by the mTAL in SS rats is an important determinant of hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ROS are important determinants of renal medullary blood supply, sodium excretion and hypertension.
the mTAL is a key player in the regulation of sodium excretion, medullary flow rate, and blood pressure, in part by its production of ROS.
the mTAL is a key site for the generation of ROS, which can regulate medullary blood supply, sodium excretion rate, and blood pressure.
